I live in Buffalo, and while it gets a bad rap it really is a great place to live, assuming you know you can get a job here. Not a huge city like NYC or LA but pretty good sized, people are generally friendly here as well. It does get pretty cold in the winter but besides a freak blizzard we never have any major weather problems at all. Summers are pretty perfect weather wise, usually in the high 70's. Not a crazy happening nightlife but there is plenty of stuff to do, especially on Elmwood. Another big plus is that cost of living is extremely low here. Buying a 2,000 square foot house in a nice neighborhood shouldn't run you more that 200,000 dollars tops.

If you want to drink, Canada has an age of 19 limit so it's always a good time when you go over with friends. There are tons of things to do down there, as they know kids come over all the time. There are weekly concerts in Lewiston Artpark and on the river front during the summer. Elmwood is the place when you are legal with lots of bars and stuff to do, while Chippewa caters to younger kids. There are lots of events that go on during the year such as various festivals and the fair. We have a few cool museums as well such as the Buffalo Museum of Science, the Albright-Knox Art Gallery, and the Naval park. We even have a nice beach in Woodlawn/Hamburg. Also, I would highly recommend going to a Bills game. We have a ton of optimism this season and the fans are always electric and loud.

As far as the weather goes, you just kind of get used to it. The only major thin is make sure you don't have a rear wheel drive car.
